issues.detail: The TeX says that fit data with t_hold < 75 ms were excluded, but supplies neither the fit endpoint nor the sampled hold times. This is not a finite common query domain and does not justify extrapolating the fitted law to every t_hold >= 75 ms.

The TeX reports only the decay time constants. It states qualitatively that the branches have different initial lattice atom numbers but gives neither numerical initial amplitude, so N_trapped(t_hold) cannot be decoded for either branch. Replacing it with normalized survival would introduce a readout that the frozen TeX does not directly report.

The source calls 54 ms and 220 ms estimated lifetimes but gives no confidence interval, standard error, covariance, residual model, or raw-count uncertainty for these fits. The source packet therefore cannot support calibrated uncertainty for generated evidence.

The two branches are real configurations, but they jointly change dimensionality, wavelength, polarization, power, detuning, lattice depth, overlap, and loading procedure. The source itself attributes the lifetime difference to depth and resonant-scattering/heating differences. A case must not present this pair as an isolated effect of 3D versus 1D geometry.

cond_1D_lattice calls the 1D lattice far-off-resonant, but its attached locator is only lines 76-77; the explicit far-detuned statement occurs at lines 94-96. The statement is scientifically supported elsewhere in the packet, but the selected locator is not complete.
